title: Bastian and the patient's plaques (paraphrase D)
topic: A clinic studies amyloid deposits in a patient's biopsy: Bastian finds deposits of misfolded amyloid in dense plaques, the laboratory finds a tau protein, a scan reveals more plaques, the patient's daughter asks questions, Bastian explains the misfolding and gives the family a treatment plan

tail_E: The patient no longer recalls names and is losing his
target_note: Same target as formulations A-C: 'memory' completes 'the patient no longer recalls names and is losing his' after ten units about amyloid deposits, plaques, a tau protein and a scan. The word and its German equivalents (Gedächtnis / Erinnerung) occur nowhere in the units or the tail, and no symptom is named inside the units, so the prediction rests on the tail plus the clinical context. ' memory' is a single Pythia token (id 3541); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.29, next candidate 'voice' ~ 0.04; pilot check for tail selection only, not a result).
author: LS-NEQ stimulus bank, paraphrase D of family F20 (amyloid biopsy in the clinic, Bastian)
notes: Formulation D, domain protein_misfolding: fourth independent re-phrasing of the ten F20A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same name Bastian). Replacements include examines a biopsy in the clinic/evaluates a biopsy on the ward (untersucht in der Klinik/bewertet auf der Station), shows amyloid deposits/demonstrates amyloid deposits (zeigt/demonstriert), consist of misfolded amyloid in dense plaques/contain only misfolded amyloid in compacted plaques (bestehen aus/enthalten nur, dicht/verdichtet; the predicate keeps the lexicon word 'nur' and the adjunct the decisive 'verdichteten', so that lsne.lang_id labels them German even when the segment stands alone between English segments), the laboratory finds a tau protein in the biopsy/the lab discovers a tau protein in the sample (findet/stößt auf), requests a scan/asks for a scan (veranlasst/bittet um), reveals more plaques/brings more plaques to light (enthüllt/bringt ans Licht), asks many questions in the corridor/fires off questions in the hall (stellt viele Fragen auf dem Flur/stellt jede Menge Fragen im Flur), explains the protein's misfolding with a drawing/elucidates the protein's misfolding with a picture (erklärt/erläutert, Zeichnung/Bild), the team discusses the treatment options/the treatment team discusses the therapy options (Team, Behandlungsoptionen/Behandlungsteam, Therapieoptionen), gives the family the treatment plan/provides the family with the plan (gibt/versorgt mit). Domain vocabulary is kept in both languages: Amyloid, Ablagerungen, Plaques, Fehlfaltung, fehlgefaltet, Tauprotein; the compounds are written closed ('Amyloidablagerungen', 'Tauprotein') because lsne.lang_id splits hyphenated words and would read a stray 'Protein' as English. As in F20A/B, unit 8 avoids a segment-final bare German 'Protein' by using the genitive 'die Fehlfaltung des Proteins'. 'bewertet', 'demonstriert', 'enthalten', 'erläutert', 'diskutiert' and 'versorgt' are inseparable, 'stößt auf' and 'bittet um' take prepositional objects, 'bringt ans Licht' is a fixed phrase whose adjunct follows it; no separable verbs ('aufweisen', 'anordnen', 'aufzeigen', 'durchsprechen', 'aushändigen' avoided). Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English. 'Bastian' is labelled 'N' by lsne.lang_id (not in the lexicon's name list), which costs no accuracy.
